evidence: Kenya MOD names the Mandera–Bulahawa strategic land crossing and workbook H01/H12 name Mandera/Belet Hawo.

limitations: The PIDA Mandera map-reference point is roughly 3.6 km north of this contact. Preserve this unresolved coordinate discrepancy; do not snap or assert it is the same exact facility.

evidence: Workbook H12 and its historical source name Elwak as a Kenya-entry crossing. EUAA identifies Ceel Waaq/El Waq/El Wak aliases; the municipal source independently locates the Kenyan town.

This is a bounded review of the connected secondary corridor, excluding nearby unclassified and track contacts.
limitations: No independently published gate coordinate has been found; the municipal coordinate is a town reference several kilometres west of the frontier.
Immigration lists Elwak as proposed; historical crossing reports do not prove current formal operation.

evidence: MOD names Kiunga–Ras Kamboni among three strategic land crossings and workbook H01 names Kiunga. RUSI independently names the Kiunga–Ishakani–Ras Kamboni cross-border area.
OSM tertiary E865 way 34359141 crosses this frontier between Ishakani and Ras Kamboni; its stored extent runs from [41.5,-1.7156867] toward [41.5855067,-1.636203].
The exception is only this specific existing road way. Its OSM Class E label does not extend the global filter to all tertiary or local roads.
limitations: No independent exact gate coordinate is available. Source pairing and OSM corridor alignment support investigation; exact post identity remains provisional.
Retained border-band graph does not include the full road continuation to Kiunga town; do not infer missing shared-node joins.
Formal sustained-transition diagnostics are required on the scoped extraction.

limits: Exact road IDs qualify only for this source-backed named-post review. Accepting an extraction exception does not accept an event link or exact gate identity.
